segments: after the ten years that he was in exile.
And he killed Leontius and Apsimar, and many of the nobles,
and he cleared the Roman administration of the patricians {OCR? / Greeks}.
And he found six thousand Arab captives,
and he released them to their country.
And he sent a large army to bring his wife and also his son,
and all of them perished in the surges of the sea.
Now when the Khagan heard, he sent and rebuked him, saying:
"You ought to have sent only a few men.
What did you think,
that I would withhold her from you? By no means,
by the life of your madness,
I will not withhold her."
Then Justinian was ashamed,
and he sent a few men, and they brought her and her son with her.
And in the year
[1017] the Arabs rebuilt the walls of Mopsuestia,
and placed a garrison in it,
and made it a watch-post on the Roman border.
And that King Abd al-Malik went to it,
and there he died. After Abd al-Malik son of Marwan, his son Walid [ruled] for nine years and five months.
He sent an army with Maslama,
and they struck against Tyana (Adana?), a city of Cappadocia,
and they waged war against it for nine months.
And Justinian sent a Roman army,
and when they met the Arabs, the Romans were defeated,
and about forty thousand of them fell.
And the Arabs captured it and plundered it.
And in the year 1022,
he captured also other many fortresses,
I think it is Ablasthin, which is Sebasteia {OCR: Sebastepolis?}, which is on the border of the Romans.
And in the sixth year of Walid,
which is the year 1022
[1022] of the Greeks, Philippicus rebelled,
and killed Justinian, king of the Romans, and Tiberius his son,
and he himself reigned.
And he also expelled the Armenians who were in his dominion,
and the Arabs settled them in Melitene and its region and in Fourth Armenia.
And the Armenians became helpers to the Arabs
and opponents of the Romans.
He was steeped in pagan {external} philosophy,
and wanted to reject the Sixth Synod, which had confirmed the dogma of Maximus of two wills.
And when he had reigned two years and six months,
the Romans overthrew him
and blinded his eyes.
that there are in Christ two wills,
one divine and the other human,
as he was (Luke
42) {note}.
notes: 1020 of the Greeks, Maslama conquered Tyana and stationed an Arab garrison in it.
